text: What kind of claim do you need to make?
hint: This decides which part of the tool applies. Only causal claims need a counterfactual design; description and prediction have their own, different standards.
options: describe=Describe what is happening, or who is affected | predict=Predict who is likely to experience an outcome | causal=Establish whether an intervention caused a change

text: Is the intervention clearly defined and documented?
hint: What it consists of, who delivers it, and at what intensity. Without this, an observed effect cannot be attributed to the intervention rather than to variation in delivery.
options: yes=Yes — specified and documented | partial=Partly — being developed | no=No

text: Does a theory of change or logic model exist?
hint: A causal model linking the intervention to expected outcomes. Without one it is unclear what the evaluation should measure or how to interpret what it finds.
options: yes=Yes — documented | partial=Partly — in development | no=No

text: Is the intervention operating at sufficient scale and maturity?
hint: Evaluating impact while delivery is still stabilising risks measuring the immaturity of the intervention rather than its effectiveness.
options: yes=Yes — stable and at scale | partial=Partly — scaling or still changing | no=No — early or small-scale

text: Can the evaluation be planned before the intervention reaches participants?
hint: Randomised designs require allocation to be decided in advance. If the intervention has already rolled out, only observational designs remain available.
options: yes=Yes — the evaluation can be designed in advance | no=No — the intervention has already been delivered or allocated
used_by: encouragement rct_cluster rct_crossover rct_individual rct_stepped_wedge rct_waitlist

text: What barriers are there to randomising who receives the intervention?
hint: Ethical, legal, political or operational. Many common objections are addressed by a design adaptation rather than by abandoning randomisation.
options: none=None identified | some=Some, likely addressable by design adaptation | high=Significant | impossible=Randomisation is ruled out

text: What is the natural unit of allocation?
hint: Where the intervention is delivered to whole sites, classes or caseloads, individuals within them cannot be allocated separately.
options: individual=Individual people | cluster=Groups — sites, teams, areas or caseloads | either=Either is possible

text: How many clusters could be allocated?
hint: For a cluster design, precision is governed by the number of clusters far more than by the number of people within them.
asked_when: allocation_unit is one of “Groups — sites, teams, areas or caseloads” or “Either is possible”
options: many=40 or more | moderate=Roughly 15 to 40 | few=Fewer than 15

text: Is there a phased rollout whose order you could set?
hint: Where everyone is treated eventually but not at once, randomising the order gives a stepped-wedge design without withholding the intervention from anyone.
options: yes=Yes — the order is ours to decide | partly=Partly — some influence over sequencing | no=No — the order is fixed or externally determined

text: Would delaying the intervention for part of the group be acceptable?
hint: Everyone receives the intervention; some receive it later, forming a temporary comparison.
options: yes=Yes — a delay is tolerable | unclear=Unclear — needs discussion | no=No — delay is not acceptable

text: Does the outcome return to baseline once the intervention stops?
hint: Required for a crossover design, where participants act as their own control.
options: yes=Yes — the effect does not persist | unclear=Unclear | no=No — effects persist or accumulate

text: Can a washout period be built in between conditions?
hint: A gap long enough for the first condition's effect to dissipate before the second begins.
asked_when: outcome_reversible is one of “Yes — the effect does not persist” or “Unclear”
options: yes=Yes | unclear=Unclear | no=No

text: Is there a way to encourage take-up without assigning the intervention itself?
hint: An invitation, reminder or incentive offered at random. Useful where the intervention cannot be withheld but take-up is voluntary.
options: yes=Yes — a credible encouragement exists | unclear=Possibly — needs exploration | no=No

text: Is there genuine uncertainty about whether the intervention works?
hint: Randomisation is hard to justify where the intervention is already known to be effective or known to be harmful.
options: yes=Yes — the effect is genuinely uncertain | unclear=Contested among stakeholders | no=No — the effect is considered established

text: Is the intervention assigned by a score, date or threshold?
hint: An eligibility cutoff on a continuous measure — a risk score, an age, an income boundary. Those just either side of it are comparable.
options: yes=Yes — a documented cutoff exists | possible=Possibly — needs investigation | no=No

text: How strictly is the cutoff followed in practice?
hint: Strict enforcement gives a sharp design. Partial compliance gives a fuzzy design, which estimates an effect only for those whose treatment the cutoff actually changed.
asked_when: assignment_threshold is one of “Yes — a documented cutoff exists” or “Possibly — needs investigation”
options: sharp=Strictly — the cutoff determines treatment | fuzzy=Mostly — the cutoff shifts the probability of treatment | unclear=Not yet established

text: Could people position themselves either side of the cutoff?
hint: If the score can be influenced by those it affects, the comparison breaks down. A density test checks for bunching at the cutoff.
asked_when: assignment_threshold is one of “Yes — a documented cutoff exists” or “Possibly — needs investigation”
options: no_evidence=Tested — no evidence of sorting | untested=Not yet tested | suspected=Sorting is likely or demonstrated

text: How many observations fall close to the cutoff?
hint: Only observations near the cutoff identify the effect. The total sample is not the relevant quantity here.
asked_when: assignment_threshold is one of “Yes — a documented cutoff exists” or “Possibly — needs investigation”
options: many=Many | some=Some | few=Few

text: Is there a factor that shifts take-up but has no other route to the outcome?
hint: Distance to a service, a lottery, an administrative quirk. Its credibility rests on an argument about mechanism, not on a statistical test.
options: yes=Yes — a candidate instrument exists | possible=Possibly — needs investigation | no=No

text: How strongly does that factor predict take-up?
hint: A weak instrument gives badly behaved estimates. The conventional first-stage F above 10 is a rule of thumb, and a contested one.
asked_when: instrument_available is one of “Yes — a candidate instrument exists” or “Possibly — needs investigation”
options: strong=Strongly | weak=Weakly | untested=Not yet established

text: Can you argue the factor affects the outcome only through take-up?
hint: This cannot be tested. It is defended on substantive grounds, and it is where most instrumental-variable designs fail.
asked_when: instrument_available is one of “Yes — a candidate instrument exists” or “Possibly — needs investigation”
options: defensible=Yes — a clear substantive argument exists | doubtful=Doubtful — plausible alternative routes exist | unassessed=Not yet considered

text: How much outcome data do you have from before the intervention?
hint: Pre-intervention periods are what make a trend testable rather than assumed. One period permits a difference but allows no check on whether the groups were moving together.
options: many=Several periods | few=Two or three periods | one=One period only | none=None
used_by: did_2x2 did_staggered its its_controlled matching rdit synth

text: Is there a group that did not receive the intervention but is otherwise similar?
hint: Another region, service, cohort or eligibility group facing comparable conditions.
options: yes=Yes — a credible comparison exists | possible=Possibly — needs investigation | no=No

text: Did the two groups move together before the intervention?
hint: The central assumption of a difference-based design. It is examined in the pre-period, never proved — the periods after the intervention are exactly what cannot be checked.
asked_when: pre_periods is one of “Several periods” or “Two or three periods”
options: supported=Yes — examined and consistent | untested=Not yet examined | violated=No — the trends clearly diverge

text: Did different groups start at different times?
hint: Variation in start dates can strengthen a design, but it also makes the conventional estimator unreliable, so it changes which estimator is appropriate.
options: yes=Yes — adoption was staggered | planned=Planned but not yet begun | no=No — a single common start date

text: Are there untreated units that resemble the treated one?
hint: A synthetic control builds a comparison by weighting several untreated units. It needs enough candidates for the weighted combination to track the treated unit beforehand.
asked_when: comparison_group is one of “Yes — a credible comparison exists” or “Possibly — needs investigation” or “No”
options: yes=Yes — a reasonable pool exists | limited=A few, of uncertain comparability | no=No comparable units

text: Is there an equivalent time series for an unaffected group?
hint: A control series distinguishes a change caused by the intervention from one that was happening anyway.
options: yes=Yes | unclear=Possibly — needs investigation | no=No

text: Is the date the intervention took effect precisely known?
hint: Required where the comparison is between the periods either side of a change.
options: yes=Yes — a specific date | approximate=Approximately — phased or uncertain | no=No

text: Did anything else change at the same time?
hint: Other policies, funding changes or external shocks coinciding with the intervention cannot be separated from it in a time-series comparison.
options: none_known=Nothing else identified | possible=Possibly — not yet checked | known=Yes — other changes coincided

text: How much do you know about the characteristics of both groups?
hint: Adjustment can only account for what is measured. The question is whether you hold the variables that drove who received the intervention.
options: rich=Extensive, for treated and untreated alike | partial=Some, with known gaps | sparse=Little

text: Do treated and untreated units actually resemble each other?
hint: Where no untreated unit resembles a treated one, no comparison exists for it. This is positivity, and it is checked rather than assumed.
asked_when: covariate_richness is one of “Extensive, for treated and untreated alike” or “Some, with known gaps”
options: good=Good — the groups overlap substantially | limited=Limited — overlap only in part of the range | poor=Poor — the groups barely overlap | untested=Not yet examined

text: Are the main reasons people received the intervention captured in your data?
hint: List the drivers of selection, then check which you actually hold. What is left over is what adjustment cannot fix.
options: all_identified=The main drivers are measured | some_unmeasured=Some known drivers are not measured | unknown=Not yet established

text: Does treatment at one point change the factors that drive later treatment?
hint: Common in ongoing services, where a response to the intervention affects whether it continues. Conventional adjustment is biased here, in either direction.
options: yes=Yes — treatment and confounders evolve together | unclear=Unclear | no=No — treatment is a one-off

text: Do you hold repeated measures of treatment and of the confounders over time?
hint: Required to model the feedback between treatment and the factors that affect it.
asked_when: time_varying_confounding is one of “Yes — treatment and confounders evolve together” or “Unclear”
options: yes=Yes — at several time points | no=No

text: How many time points do you have before and after the intervention?
hint: A trend has to be estimated on each side of the interruption. Roughly eight points per segment is a common minimum, and a convention rather than a derived figure.
options: many=Eight or more each side | moderate=Roughly four to eight each side | few=Fewer than four each side

text: Is there a plan to account for correlation between adjacent time points?
hint: Observations close in time resemble each other. Ignoring this makes the effect look more precisely estimated than it is.
options: yes=Yes — it will be modelled | unclear=Not yet decided | no=No

text: Can you speak to the people who deliver and receive the intervention?
hint: Required to elicit how the intervention is meant to work, and for whom.
options: yes=Yes | limited=Limited | no=No

text: Is there documentation covering each step of the intended causal chain?
hint: Records, monitoring data, case files or correspondence evidencing what happened at each stage.
options: yes=Yes — substantial | limited=Patchy | no=No
